content_preview.title: Dart 3.14 Adds dart migrate and Hardware WebAssembly SIMD and Marks FFIgen for Objective-C and JNIgen Stable; Its Changelog Lists Breaking Changes
content_preview.summary: Dart's blog post dated November 11 lists dart migrate, WebAssembly SIMD and stable FFIgen for Objective-C and JNIgen; the 3.14.0 changelog also lists breaking changes to SIMD types and unshipped Isolate APIs.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Dart team published a blog post dated November 11, 2026 announcing Dart 3.14. The post, [Announcing Dart 3.14](https://dart.dev/blog/announcing-dart-3-14) by Connie Ooi, lists a new `dart migrate` command, a beta of a re-engineered DartPad, hardware 128-bit WebAssembly SIMD in the `dart2wasm` compiler, and FFIgen for Objective-C and JNIgen as stable. The [3.14.0 changelog on GitHub](https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/blob/3.14.0/CHANGELOG.md) also contains, by the Herald's count, ...

recommendations: No corrections needed. The independent-source requirement applies to Analysis only; the article states its first-party sourcing in its closing section.

editor_notes.content_quality: Release News piece of 1,057 words (400-1,200 range). Structure: lead, what the announcement lists, what the changelog adds, dates and browser floors, and a closing section stating what the sources do not settle. The cross-check of the announcement against the 3.14.0 changelog is the article's value, and it is reproducible from primary records. Own derivations are labelled 'by the Herald's count/calculation'. Neutral tone, no AI self-reference, no promotional language.
editor_notes.source_verification: Anthropic disclosure: not required - Anthropic and Claude are not mentioned in the headline, summary, lead or body. First-party sourcing: config/editorial_policy.md requires 3-5 sources for News (this article cites 11) and requires independent sources only for Analysis (at least 2 independent of the subject); it states a preference for reputable outlets but sets no independence floor for News. Independent-source count: 0 outlets; the only non-project items are MDN browser-compat-data JSON (data, pinned to commit 69fcf36, two files). The article states this plainly ('Apart from the MDN data, every cited page comes from the Dart and Flutter projects' own sites and repository'), attributes every vendor figure to Dart ('These are Dart's figures'), and the headline attributes the breaking-change claim ('Its Changelog Lists'). I judged first-party-only acceptable here because every checkable claim is verifiable from primary records (tag, commit, changelog, issues), the article is a comparison of two primary records, and the limits are disclosed. A web search for outside coverage could not be run (search budget exhausted), so the 'found and cites no outside report' statement is accepted as the Herald's own scoped statement. Snapshots read from sources/2026-11/<slug>/ (gunzip, text extraction): source-0 dart.dev blog (sha256 ba6389ed..., live re-fetch with browser User-Agent byte-identical): dated 'Nov 11, 2026', author Connie Ooi, 'the new dart migrate tool', 'Hardware 128-bit WebAssembly SIMD' section, 'With Dart 3.14, FFIgen for Objective-C and JNIgen are stable!', Chrome 137+/Safari 26.2+/Firefox 147+, ETag 144 dependencies ~1.5 MB, DartPad beta, legacy libraries 'scheduled for removal ... in an upcoming release'; text search of the page for breaking/V128/toString/NaN/IEEE/isolate/runSync/unship/experimental returns nothing (only 'min read' and 'Dart SDK changelog' link), so 'none of the three mentioned' holds. source-1 flutter.dev: dated Nov 11, 2026, 'FFIgen for Objective-C and JNIgen for Java and Kotlin join FFIgen's long-standing C support as stable', Safari 26.2+/Firefox 147+ opt-in via wasmAllowList 'before they become enabled by default in a future stable release', 'will be removed in a future Dart release'. source-2 CHANGELOG.md at 3.14.0: the GitHub HTML snapshot is a JavaScript shell, so I read the raw file via raw.githubusercontent.com/dart-lang/sdk/3.14.0/CHANGELOG.md (curl, browser UA, HTTP 200, sha256 ab9db5100a32c34628afa3b9a67407ca4c66200001a0b1072f5986cc3c99bef2). The 3.14.0 section contains exactly 3 'Breaking change' labels (case-insensitive search for 'breaking' finds only these): dart:isolate unshipped APIs (8 named, plus NativeCallable.isolateGroupBound gated behind --experimental-shared-data), SIMD toString() -> 'V128', SIMD min/max IEEE 754. 'Released on: Unreleased' confirmed at the tag. The same section lists 'Added a `dart migrate` command' and dart2wasm hardware v128 SIMD. 3.13.0 section: 'Added synchronous execution and event loop control APIs to `Isolate`' naming the same 8 APIs; 3.13.1-3.13.7 sections do not mention Isolate. source-3 dart.dev/tools/dart-migrate: Dart 3.0 or later, 'It doesn't upgrade the Dart or Flutter SDK installed on your machine', no uncommitted-change check, cleanups listed in summary not applied by default, does not expand Pub workspaces, 'Page last updated on 2026-11-04'. source-4 dart.dev/web/wasm: 'Chrome or Edge 137+ / Safari 26.2+ / Firefox 134+ (or 147+ for Flutter web)', 'Page last updated on 2026-11-10'. source-5 issue #63962: closed 2026-10-06, opened by modulovalue 2026-08-04 who leans to option 1 (IEEE semantics, a breaking change); quoted sentence verbatim. source-6 issue #64285: opened 2026-09-15T13:32Z by mraleph, still open on 2026-11-15 (re-checked with the GitHub API), quote 'we by accident shipped experimental Isolate and FFI apis' verbatim, and the issue asks to cherry-pick into stable but no cited page says it was done. source-7 tag page: datetime 2026-11-11T08:24:12Z (git tag object tagger date identical, tagger 'Dart CI'). source-8 commit fa8c127: title 'Version 3.14.0', message 'Merge 3.14.0-315.3.beta into stable'; GitHub API author/committer date 2026-11-05T00:28:39Z = 2026-11-04 16:28 UTC-08:00; gap to the tag 6 days 7 h 55 min ('about six days'). source-9 and source-10 MDN BCD JSON: jsStringBuiltins Chrome 130 / Firefox 134 / Safari 26.2; exceptionsFinal Chrome 137 / Firefox 131 / Safari 18.4, so the larger-of-two values equal Chrome 137, Firefox 134, Safari 26.2 as the article states (the docs also list WasmGC as a third requirement, which the article does not claim to cover). Each of the 11 sources confirmed the claims attributed to it. Allowlist: dart.dev, flutter.dev, github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com are all on config/source_allowlist.txt; no additions. Prompt-injection scanner: one match on source-2 (override-instructions), excerpt "(and the corresponding parameter in any method that overrides it) has looser"," override rules. In strong mode, these require a runtime type check to maintain"," soundness"; in the raw changelog it is line 10543-10546, a very old entry introducing the covariant modifier ('It indicates that the parameter (and the corresponding parameter in any method that overrides it) has looser override rules'), which is Dart language documentation and not an instruction to a reader. False positive; no other snapshot or raw page matches an instruction-to-agent search. Extra context not cited by the article: the Dart SDK archive VERSION file (storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive/channels/stable/release/3.14.0/VERSION, last-modified 2026-11-11 08:26 GMT) lists version 3.14.0, date 2026-11-04, revision fa8c127, consistent with the article's dates; docs.flutter.dev/platform-integration/web/wasm says 'Firefox < 147 automatically falls back to dart2js + CanvasKit', which explains the Flutter-web 147 floor (the article only says the cited pages do not say why, which is true of its own cited pages).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Headline: 'Adds dart migrate' (new command per blog and changelog 'Added a `dart migrate` command'); 'Hardware WebAssembly SIMD' (blog heading 'Hardware 128-bit WebAssembly SIMD', changelog 'hardware 128-bit WebAssembly SIMD (v128)'); 'Marks FFIgen for Objective-C and JNIgen Stable' (blog wording, Flutter post wording); 'Its Changelog Lists Breaking Changes' (3 labelled entries). Summary and lead consistent with these and attributed to the blog post dated November 11. All 18 quoted strings re-matched against raw page text (16 on the cited pages verbatim, 'Released on: Unreleased' is the rendered form of '**Released on:** Unreleased', 'Breaking change' is the label text). Claim-accuracy tests: absence claims ('none of the three mentioned', 'no cited page gives a version or date for removing the legacy web libraries', 'do not mention it' for 3.13.1-3.13.7) hold against every cited source and are scoped to the cited pages; derived figures (three entries, eight APIs, 'about six days', UTC conversion, browser maxima) recomputed and correct; the Firefox 134 vs 147 disagreement is reported with attribution; vendor figures (up to 4x, ~1.5 MB) are labelled as Dart's; release dates and time-zone basis are stated. No quantifier overreach found.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and descriptive; the closing section lists what the sources do not settle without speculation.
editor_notes.originality: No earlier Herald article covers Dart 3.14 (the only recent Dart item is the TIOBE ranking story, a different subject).

editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-scoped release coverage whose cross-check of the announcement against the changelog (three breaking changes the announcement does not mention) is verifiable from primary records and honestly framed. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid, accurate release story for Dart and Flutter developers
